newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity up along with higher physicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity up along with higher physicals.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading higher Tuesday in line with stronger physical power prices in the U.S. West, industry sources said.
Cash power values were said to be up in part on a one-week delay in restarting the San Onofre 3 nuclear power unit in California, the sources said.
"The daily market is up again today," said one futures trader.

As of 1220 EDT, August Palo Verde (PV) futures were up 85 cents at $35.95 per megawatt hour (MWh) following exchanges at $35.55-36.10, while September was up 59 cents at the day's high of $29.85 after exchanges as low as $29.50 per MWh.

August California Oregon Border (COB) was trading up 34 cents at $23.50 following exchanges in a range of $23.40-23.60, while September was up 33 cents at the day's low of $23.21 after reaching as high as $23.30 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1140 EDT an estimated total of 283 PV and 52 COB contracts had traded.
NYMEX natural gas futures were also trading higher Tuesday, up 4.2 cents at $2.11 per million British thermal units as of 1220 EDT.

In generation news, the 750 megawatt (MW) unit 2 at the Mohave coal-fired power plant in Nevada was expected to come back on line late Wednesday night after tripping off-line Monday. The unit was down due to a boiler tube leak. The plant's other 750 MW unit was said to be operating normally.
Also, the 1,073 MW unit 2 at the Diablo Canyon nuclear power plant was expected to reach full power by Tuesday evening, Pacific Gas & Electric Co, the plant's operator said.

The unit, located at Avila Beach on California's central coast, was operating at 75 percent power after being manually shut early Wednesday due to a problem with its feedwater system, the company said.

Strength in daily power prices was seen in part from a SoCal Edison decision Monday to delay the restart of its 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 nuclear unit by a week to July 17. Engineers needed time to replace the unit's instrument nozzles.
The unit, in San Clemente, Calif., has been offline since April 12 for refueling and maintenance.
SoCal Edison added the adjacent 1,080 MW unit 2 was still on schedule to return to service near July 10 after being shut June 29 to replace charge line check valves.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state hit 15 percent power early today but had not yet reconnected to the electricity grid.
Wet and cool weather was expected in the Pacific Northwest into the weekend before a warming trend was forecast for early next week.
Temperatures were projected to average near normal over most of the Southwest but below normal in the far northeast region and above normal in the extreme southwest area.
